text:
maya: quick triage - onboarding Hypha-7B (Llama FF + Mistral-style attention). conversion + int4 done. Long-doc summarization falls apart after ~800 tokens.
liam: numbers?
maya: rouge-L down ~13 vs fp16 on our 3k-docs; ppl jumps ~45 at 3k. short contexts fine.
jorge: usual suspects: head ordering, rotary base/freq, tokenizer normalization. Any converter warnings?
maya: converter log had: 
``nWARN: inferred_head_layout=interleaved stride=2
WARN: rotary_base: missing per-block, defaulting to 10000
``
nora: interleaved stride=2 -> possible head permutation. If we flattened without permuting, q/k/v ordering mismatch.
sami: did you run per-head cosine between fp16 and int4 attention projections?
maya: yep. Layers 6-9 show ~0.80 mean cosine, rest >0.98. also kv_cosine vs timestep: layer8 t0=0.996 t256=0.932 t512=0.694 t800=0.412.
liam: that decaying curve screams rotary phase mismatch not quant noise alone. Any per-layer rotary info in the source model card?
maya: model card has "rotary_frequencies": [10000, 5000], and a note "layers 6-9 use second group". converter ignored unknown field.
jorge: OK that matches. If we applied 10000 everywhere, layers expecting 5000 will accumulate phase error with position. Permuting heads fixed short-context but long still off.
nora: try two fixes: 1) patch converter to read per-layer rotary_frequencies and emit per-layer metadata 2) allow per-channel quant calibration for attention projections on affected layers.
sami: also check tokenizer. I saw Hypha tokenizer normalizes U+200C and has special BOS mapping for some datasets. If tokenizer output shifts at high indices, that will amplify rotor misalignment.
maya: I ran token diff on a long doc. found a single split at pos ~812 that shifts subsequent ids by +1 for ~180 tokens. converter version 0.3.0 had a pad sentinel off-by-one bug; fixed in 0.3.1.
liam: so compounding issues: head interleave + missing rotary group + token id shift. All amplify in long runs.
jorge: for calibration, try per-channel symmetric quant for q/k/v/out and also per-head clamp on the tiny-magnitude rotary-projection columns. Int4 tends to lose small-scale rotaries.
nora: add preflight checks: kv_cosine curve fp16->quant up to t=1024 (fail if any layer <0.9 at t=256), token_alignment test (require <0.1% token id drift on long sample), and a head-permutation checksum artifact in model tar when permutation applied.
maya: quick experiment: re-export with per-layer freq (layers 6-9 -> 5000), enforced contiguous head order, int4 per-channel calibrate for affected layers. Rouge-L recovered +9 (still -4 vs fp16). kv_cosine for layer8 improved: t0=0.997 t256=0.978 t512=0.901 t800=0.742.
sami: big win. Remaining gap probably quant granularity interacting with small-frequency rotaries. Try int4 fallback for those layers or micro-bucket calibration.
liam: agree. Also add an automated onboarding guard: when new model is added, run a short long-doc probe (3k tokens) in CI and require no more than 3pt rouge-L regression vs fp16 baseline.
jorge: for rollout: canary on Dedicated, 8% traffic with synthetic long-doc probes every 30s. automatic rollback if rouge-L drops >3 pts over 15m.
ciabot: maya pushed branch "hypha/rotary-freq-tokenfix-calib" with 4 commits. CI queued.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled on eng-dedicated at 2026-05-02T12:00:00Z routing 8% to model:hypha-7b:v2-canary. Automatic rollback enabled.
maya: I'll finish the converter patch to read rotary_frequencies and emit permutation map. will upload kv_cosine plots to the model registry once CI finishes.
liam: happy to help run micro-bucket calibration tomorrow.
maya: thanks all. will report back after canary.
